assertions.name: two_is_the_unique_graded_prime
assertions.source: p=2 carries the exact ℤ/2 parity grading (v2(den b_k)=0 ⟺ k odd, with the a_k mirror), while p=3 is ungraded factorial-smooth growth (v3(den b_k)>0 on both parities) — 2 = the bar-involution prime is the unique prime that sees the grading

description: Sharpens the D-ladder 2-adic parity grading (PR #3737, Result 2): among all primes dividing den(d_k), p=2 is the UNIQUE graded prime (v2(den b_k)=0 ⟺ k odd; the singular 2-adic mass swaps to a_k on the other parity), while p=3 (and 5,7,…) are ungraded factorial-smooth (Ohtsuki–Habiro) growth ~1.4k regardless of parity. 2 is the prime of the ℤ/2 bar-involution, so only it sees the grading. Exact p-adic valuations of the exact ℚ(√3) coefficients; no fit, no c_k wired, no tier change.
